JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.12,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 13-10-2021 at about 12:10 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on Honda Activa Scooter bearing No.KA-04-JX-4095, from Magadi road towards Pipe lane, near Tent road, Sunkadakatte, Bengaluru.
At that time, the rider of said scooter rode the same with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life, lost control over the vehicle and fell down on the road.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on his left leg and right hand.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Smt. Jayadevi Memorial Hospital,
Chikkagollarahatti, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as cab driver and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Kamakshipalya Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said scooter for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.2 is the owner and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and Raghu Kumar.S vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85204733/
2 award compensation of Rs.12,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.

sentences.text: 3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.3 appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondent No.2 is placed as ex-parte.
4. The respondent No.3 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04-JX-4095 and it has issued the Bundled Two Wheeler policy covering for the period 20-06-2019 to 19-06- 2020 for own damage and 20-06-2019 to 19-06-2024 for liability only cover.
The pillion rider is not covered during the 2nd year, more particular at the time of the accident.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act.

It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6)
of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the rider of Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-53- 6331 was not holding valid and effective driving licence, as on the date of accident.
The petitioner himself was riding the vehicle and he was solely negligent in causing the accident.

However, the petitioner in order to get unlawful gain has created false story of alleged accident and falsely implicated the rider of the insured vehicle, by misrepresenting the material facts with regard to the alleged accident.
The rider of the vehicle was not covered under the policy, as on the date of alleged accident.
As such the claim petition is not maintainable for one's own negligence.
Further it is contended that, the rider of the alleged Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04-JX-4095 was no way involved in the alleged accident.
The jurisdictional police have filed the false charge-sheet against the said vehicle, colluding with the claimant and owner of the vehicle.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further it has contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 13-10-2021 at about 12.10 p.m., due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Activa Honda Scooter bearing Reg.
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3
. What order or Award ?

the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

sentences.text: The petitioner has deposed that, earlier to the accident, he was working as cab driver and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his learning capacity.

But, the petitioner has neither produced any document nor examined any doctor to establish that, due to injuries sustained in the accident in question, he has suffered any physical disability or deformity.

The petitioner has failed to prove that, due to accidental injuries he has suffered physical disability and he is not in a position to continue his avocation or perform his regular work and thereby, he has lost his learning capacity.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation under head loss of future income due to permanent physical disability does not arise at all.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
ii) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 2 medical bills, as per Ex.P.9.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.1,39,851/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,39,851/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:
In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e. fracture tibial plateau left leg with fracture distal radius right.

As per Ex.P.8 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 9 days from 13-10-2021 to 21-10- 2021, in Smt.
Jayadevi Memorial Hospital, Chikkagollarahatti, Bengaluru.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.40,000/-
is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.8 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 9 days in Smt. Jayadevi Memorial Hospital, Chikkagollarahatti, Bengaluru.

compensation of Rs.1000 x 9 = Rs.9,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.

Therefore,
compensation of Rs.800 x 9 = Rs.7,200/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.

sentences.text: The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before the accident he was working as cab driver and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent No.3 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was working as cab driver and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident has taken place in the year 2021.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,000/- per month.

The petitioner has taken treatment for 9 days as in-patient at Smt. Jayadevi Memorial Hospital,
Chikkagollarahatti, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries caused to him.
He might have taken rest for about 2 months and lost his income for the said period.
Therefore, Rs.15,000 x 2 = Rs.30,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 35 years and unfortunately he has suffered grievous injuries in the said accident and undergone treatment for 9 days as in-patient in Smt. Jayadevi Memorial Hospital, Chikkagollarahatti, Bengaluru.
Further, it might have took 2 months for complete curing of the injuries suffered by him.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities during the treatment period would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses: The petitioner has neither adduced any evidence nor produced any document to show that he requires any further treatment for the injuries sustained in the accident.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation for future medical expenses does not arise at all.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded in this particular head.

20. Liability: Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2 is the owner and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-04-JX-4095 the said accident has occurred.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.

The respondent No.3 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
21.

But, the respondent No.3 has taken specific contention that, it has issued the Bundled Two Wheeler policy in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of offending Honda Active Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04-JX-4095, which covers risk of own damage for the period from 20-06-2019 to 19-06-2020 and third party liability for the period from 20-06-2019 to 19-06-2024.

Further it has contended that, the own damage liability and liability of pillion rider was not covered as on the date of accident, as the own damage risk coverage was only for the period from 20-06-2019 to 19-06- 2020.

Further, the learned counsel for respondent No.3 has vehemently argued that, as per the Ex.R.1 insurance policy issued by the respondent No.3 insurance company in respect of offending Honda Active Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04-JX-4095, the liability of pillion rider was not covered,
as no additional premium with respect to risk coverage of pillion rider has been collected from the insured.

Further he has argued that, it is settled proposition of law that, the pillion rider of a two-wheeler cannot to be treated as third party, when the accident has taken place self rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending two- wheeler and there is no other vehicle involved in the said accident.

In support of his arguments the learned counsel has relied on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Madras, in the case of Pula Shanmugam and another V/s Yugender Ravellah and others, in CMA No.2093/2023, dated 29-01-2025, wherein it is clearly held that, "The current legal position is that, the pillion rider is not covered under third party insurance unless an additional premium in this regard was paid.

entities.text: Pula Shanmugam and another V/s Yugender Ravellah and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The deceased being a pillion rider can claim neither under own damage nor third party coverage."

22. On meticulously going through the Ex.R.1 insurance policy it clearly reveals that, no additional premium has been collected in respect of risk coverage of the pillion liability and as such it does not cover the liability of pillion rider.
Further it reveals that, even the own damage coverage was not valid as on the date of accident, as the own damage coverage was only for the period from 20-06- 2019 to 19-06-2020.
This clearly goes to show that, as on the date of accident the Ex.R.1 insurance policy was not valid and it does not cover the risk of own damage liability or the pillion rider liability.

Further, as it is held by the Hon'ble High Court of Madras in the above cited decision, the current legal position of law is that, the pillion rider is not covered under third party insurance unless an additional premium in this regard is paid by the insured.

Therefore, in such circumstances and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the opinion that, the respondent No.3 insurance Raghu Kumar.S vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85204733/
9 company is not liable to indemnify the owner of insured vehicle i.e. respondent No.2.

The petition against respondent No.3 is dismissed.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
At that time, the rider of said scooter rode the same with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life, lost control over the vehicle and fell down on the road.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on his left leg and right hand.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Kamakshipalya Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said scooter for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.2 is the owner and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act.
opennyai_summary.issue:

No.KA-04-JX-4095 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?

. What order or Award ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Whereas, the respondent No.3 insurance company has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the offending Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04-JX-4095 by the petitioner himself and the rider shown in the charge-sheet is falsely implicated in the said accident, in collusion with the respondent No.2 and the jurisdictional police, in order to have wrongful gain from the respondent No.3 insurance company.
Except the self serving statements of the R.W.1, who is the representative/Senior Manager of respondent No.3 insurance company, there is absolutely no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by respondent No.3 to show that, the petitioner was the actual rider at the relevant point of time of accident and the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself and the petitioner in collusion with the respondent No.2 and the jurisdictional police has falsely implicated the rider shown in the charge- sheet, in order to have wrongful gain from the respondent No.3 insurance company.
When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no other vehicle involved in the accident, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending scooter.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent No.3 and even nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has occurred due to the negligence of petitioner himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.
The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.7, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04-JX-4095.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the owner or the rider of offending vehicle.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending Raghu Kumar.
S vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd
The petitioner has suffered fracture of tibial plateau left leg with fracture of distal radius right.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that,
the respondent No.3 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04-JX-4095 and injuries sustained to the petitioner in the said accident.
15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was working as cab driver and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,000/- per month.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities during the treatment period would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses: The petitioner has neither adduced any evidence nor produced any document to show that he requires any further treatment for the injuries sustained in the accident.
22. On meticulously going through the Ex.R.1 insurance policy it clearly reveals that, no additional premium has been collected in respect of risk coverage of the pillion liability and as such it does not cover the liability of pillion rider.
This clearly goes to show that, as on the date of accident the Ex.R.1 insurance policy was not valid and it does not cover the risk of own damage liability or the pillion rider liability.

19. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income -Nil- 2.
Conveyance expenses 5,000-00 7. Loss of income during 30,000-00 treatment period
Accordingly,
holding that the respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation of Rs.2,51,051/- to the petitioner, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
23. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.2,51,051/- (Rupees two lakh fifty one thousand and fifty one only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents No.2 is liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner and he is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
The petition against respondent No.3 is dismissed.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
